title: Beach Safety for Families: Flags, Rips and Lifeguards
description: Beach safety for families: lifeguarded beaches, what the red and yellow flags mean, rip currents, tides, inflatables and what to do if someone is in trouble.
intro: A few simple rules make a beach day safer for everyone. Here’s what every family should know before heading to the coast.

image.alt: Two parents and a child holding hands on the seashore

cardText: Flags, rip currents, tides and lifeguards explained.

blocks.title: Scout’s safety rule
blocks.text: Choose a lifeguarded beach and swim between the red and yellow flags. If anyone’s in trouble, call 999 and ask for the Coastguard.
points: Never swim at a red flag

sections.html:
• Red and yellow: lifeguarded area, the safest place to swim and bodyboard.
  • Black and white chequered: area for surfboards, kayaks and other craft. Don’t swim here.
  • Red: danger. Never go in the water.
  • Orange windsock: offshore winds, so don’t use inflatables.

Rips are strong currents that can drag swimmers out. The RNLI advises: if you’re caught in one, don’t try to swim against it. Swim parallel to the shore if you can, or raise a hand and shout for help. If you’re tired, float to live: lean back and float until you can breathe and swim to safety.
Check tide times before rock pooling or fossil hunting, so you don’t get cut off. Keep away from cliff edges and bases. See beaches and seaside.

faqs.q: What should you do if you see someone in trouble in the sea?
faqs.a: In the UK, call 999 and ask for the Coastguard. Don’t go in after them yourself. Throw something that floats if you can.
